questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a French candidature commits the applicant to sending
questions.stem: Item 0001 in the beekeeper's logbook asks what a French candidature commits the applicant to sending.

options.text: A CV and a cover letter are required.
Only a cover letter is required.

questions.explanation: A French candidature commits the applicant to sending both a CV and a cover letter. Sending only one is wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-french
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What the top of a French CV leads with
questions.stem: Item 0002 in the beekeeper's logbook asks what the top of a French CV leads with.

answer.exemplar: The top of a French CV leads with the applicant's identity and contact details, followed by a short professional title or objective, so the reader immediately knows who is applying and for which post.

questions.explanation: The CV opens with identity and contact details. Leading with hobbies or salary is wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-french
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The claim a French cover letter makes

stimulus.body: A French cover letter states the applicant's motivation and fit for the post. It links skills to the employer's needs. It does not repeat the CV verbatim.

questions.stem: Item 0003 in the beekeeper's logbook asks what claim a French cover letter makes.

options.text: It repeats the CV word for word.

options.misconception: focuses on pay instead of fit

options.text: It states motivation and fit for the post.

questions.explanation: The cover letter states motivation and fit. Repeating the CV or demanding salary is wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-french
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Why the opening interview question looks odd
questions.stem: Item 0004 in the beekeeper's logbook asks why the opening interview question looks odd.

options.text: It asks the candidate to present themselves.

questions.explanation: The opening question asks the candidate to present themselves, which looks odd. Salary or weakness openers are wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-french
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a formal French form of address signals
questions.stem: Item 0005 in the beekeeper's logbook asks what a formal French form of address signals.
questions.explanation: A formal form of address signals respect and social distance. Familiarity is wrong.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a non-compete clause does
questions.stem: Item 0006 in the beekeeper's logbook asks what a non-compete clause does.

answer.exemplar: A non-compete clause restricts the employee from working for a rival or starting a similar business for a set period after leaving, in exchange for compensation, and only if it is proportionate.

questions.explanation: The clause restricts rival work for a period. It does not forbid all work forever.

provenance.author: bank-team-french
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Gross pay and take-home pay

stimulus.body: Gross pay is the amount before deductions. Take-home pay is what remains after social charges. The gap between them is significant.

questions.stem: Item 0007 in the beekeeper's logbook asks which pay is received after deductions.
questions.explanation: Take-home pay is received after deductions. Gross pay is before deductions.

provenance.author: bank-team-french
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.stem: Item 0008 in the beekeeper's logbook asks how a French working day is written.

options.text: With h between hours and minutes.

questions.explanation: A French working day uses h between hours and minutes. A colon or comma is wrong.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a rotating shift post involves
questions.stem: Item 0009 in the beekeeper's logbook asks what a rotating shift post involves.
questions.explanation: A rotating shift post involves changing hours across periods. Fixed hours only is wrong.

provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The right to stop work in a dangerous situation
questions.stem: Item 0010 in the beekeeper's logbook asks about the right to stop work in a dangerous situation.

answer.exemplar: An employee may stop work when facing a serious and imminent danger to life or health, without needing prior permission, and must notify the employer and safety representatives promptly.

questions.explanation: The employee may stop work for serious imminent danger. Prior permission is not required.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a union negotiates and who it covers

stimulus.body: A union negotiates working conditions and pay. It covers employees in a sector or firm. Membership is voluntary but representation follows rules.

questions.stem: Item 0011 in the beekeeper's logbook asks who a union covers.

options.text: Employees in the sector or firm.

questions.explanation: A union covers employees in the sector or firm. Restricting to managers or members is wrong.

questions.explanation: A dismissal disagreement goes through the labour tribunal. Criminal court or police is wrong.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The usual basis of a promotion
questions.stem: Item 0014 in the beekeeper's logbook asks the usual basis of a promotion.

answer.exemplar: A promotion usually rests on a combination of seniority, competence, and performance, assessed through reviews, rather than on a single automatic criterion or favouritism.

questions.explanation: Promotion rests on seniority, competence, and performance. A single criterion is wrong.

questions.stem: Item 0015 in the beekeeper's logbook asks what a performance review must produce.

options.text: A written record and agreed goals.

questions.explanation: The review produces a written record and agreed goals. An oral chat only is wrong.

questions.stem: Item 0016 in the beekeeper's logbook asks which procedure protects an employee facing dismissal.

questions.explanation: It settles location, schedule, equipment, and costs. Leaving these open is wrong.

answer.exemplar: A service budget groups headings such as personnel, operating costs, investments, and subsidies, so that spending on a public service can be tracked and compared across periods.

questions.subject: FRENCH

questions.stem: Item 0034 in the beekeeper's logbook asks the mood required after il faut que.

answer.exemplar: After il faut que, the clause must be in the subjunctive mood, because the construction expresses necessity or obligation rather than a stated fact, so the indicative would be wrong.

questions.explanation: Il faut que requires the subjunctive. Using the indicative is wrong.
